## 1. Load libraries

```{r}
#| label: load-libraries

library(data.table)
library(susieR)
```

## 2. Load data

```{r}
#| label: load-data

expr_dt <- fread("data/student_trial_expression.txt")
pheno_dt <- fread("data/phenotypes-20260429.txt")
geno_dt <- fread("data/student_trial_genotypes.txt")
gemma_gwas_dt <- fread("data/student_trial_gemma.txt")
eqtl_dt <- fread("data/student_trial_eqtl.txt")
```

## 3. Inspect and validate the input data

### 3.1 Table dimensions and column names

```{r}
#| label: inspect-inputs

input_summary <- data.table(
  dataset = c("Expression", "Phenotypes", "Genotypes", "GWAS", "eQTL"),
  rows = c(
    nrow(expr_dt), 
    nrow(pheno_dt), 
    nrow(geno_dt), 
    nrow(gemma_gwas_dt),
    nrow(eqtl_dt)
  ),
  columns = c(
    ncol(expr_dt),
    ncol(pheno_dt), 
    ncol(geno_dt), 
    ncol(gemma_gwas_dt),
    ncol(eqtl_dt)    
  )
)

print(input_summary)

cat("\nGWAS colums:\n")
print(names(gemma_gwas_dt))

cat("\neQTL colums:\n")
print(names(eqtl_dt))
```

### 3.2 Match genotype and expression sample IDs

```{r}
#| label: validate-sample-ids

expression_samples <- names(expr_dt)[-1]
genotype_samples <- names(geno_dt)[-1]

stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(expression_samples),
  !anyDuplicated(genotype_samples)
)

sample_check <- data.table(
  check = c(
    "Expression samples",
    "Genotype samples",
    "Shared full sample IDs",
    "Same columns in the same order"
  ),
  value = c(
    length(expression_samples),
    length(genotype_samples),
    length(
      intersect(
        expression_samples,
        genotype_samples
      )
    ),
    as.character(
      identical(
        expression_samples,
        genotype_samples
      )
    )
  )
)

sample_check
```

**Observations**\
The expression and genotype tables each contain 375 samples. All 375 full sample IDs match, and the samples appear in the same column order, so these tables are aligned for the analysis. The GWAS and eQTL tables contain 292 and 11 records, respectively.

## 4. Prepare GWAS summary statistics

### 4.1 Define a helper function `prep_gemma_zscores()`

```{r}
#| label: helper-function-prep-gemma-zscores

#' Prepare GEMMA GWAS z-scores
#' 
#' Calculate a Wald-style z-score (Beta / SE) for each SNP-trait 
#' association and keep the columns needed for downstream analysis.
#'
#' @param gemma_dt A data frame or data.table containing SNP_ID, Trait, Beta, and SE columns.
#' @return  A data.table with columns id, Trait, Beta, SE, and z.
#'   Rows with missing z-scores are removed.
prep_gemma_zscores <- function(gemma_dt){
  gwas_dt <- copy(as.data.table(gemma_dt))
  gwas_dt[, z := Beta / SE]
  
  gwas_dt[
    , 
    .(
      id = SNP_ID, 
      Trait = Trait,
      Beta = Beta,
      SE = SE,
      z = z
    )
  ][!is.na(z)]
}
```

### 4.2 Inpect the resulting z-scores

```{r}
#| label: inspect-zscores

gwas_zscore <- prep_gemma_zscores(gemma_gwas_dt)

head(gwas_zscore, 10)
```

**Observations**

The GEMMA results were reduced to SNP ID, trait, effect estimate, standard error, and z-score. The z-score preserves the direction of the estimated effect and expresses its size relative to its standard error. The first ten rows include both positive and negative associations.

## 5. Define the locus fine-mapping function

### 5.1 Define helpers for the locus fine-mapping function

```{r}
#| label: helper-select-locus-genotypes

#' Select genotype rows within a genomic window
#' 
#' @param geno_dt Genotype data.table with SNP identifiers in the SNP column.
#' @param chr Chromosome identifier.
#' @param start_pos,end_pos Inclusive genomic window boundaries.
#' @return A data.table of SNPs in the window, with an added pos column.
select_locus_genotypes <- function(
    geno_dt, chr, start_pos, end_pos
){
  locus_dt <- geno_dt[grepl(paste0("^0?", chr, ":"), SNP)]
  locus_dt[, pos := as.numeric(tstrsplit(SNP, ":")[[2]])]
  locus_dt[pos >= start_pos & pos <= end_pos]
}
```
